title: Commissioning Project Manager I
description:
The Commissioning Project Manager I supports the planning, coordination, execution, and closeout of commissioning activities for assigned projects, project phases, or systems within CyrusOne's data center development portfolio. Acting as the owner's representative during commissioning activities, this role works closely with design, construction, operations, vendors, contractors, project managers, and third-party commissioning providers to support successful testing, turnover, and operational readiness.
The Commissioning Project Manager I is responsible for coordinating commissioning activities, tracking deficiencies and project risks, supporting testing readiness, and facilitating documentation and closeout requirements. The role may independently manage smaller projects or commissioning scopes while developing the skills and experience necessary to assume full project-level commissioning responsibility.

What You Will Do:
Attend meetings with design, construction, operations, and third party commissioning teams to understand project goals, schedule, and commissioning requirements and to help ensure commissioning activities are completed in alignment with project milestones.

- Participate in meetings with design, construction, operations, and third party commissioning teams to support alignment on project objectives, schedules, and commissioning requirements.

- Review commissioning related documentation, including equipment submittals, shop drawings, test scripts, operating sequences, and turnover materials, for alignment with design intent and owner requirements.

- Support the commissioning team in an owner’s representative role through document review of earlier commissioning activities and field oversight of later stage activities.

- Perform pre functional inspections, field observations, and system verification activities to confirm equipment and systems are installed in accordance with project requirements.

- Participate in functional testing of electrical, mechanical, controls, and related building systems to verify performance in accordance with approved procedures and design documents.

- Coordinate with vendors, contractors, project teams, and third party commissioning partners to support test readiness, execution, and timely resolution of issues.

- Track commissioning deficiencies, open items, and retesting requirements through resolution and closeout, and communicate status and risks to project stakeholders.

- Support construction, project management, and operations teams in resolving issues that may affect startup, testing, turnover, or operational readiness.

- Review operating modes, sequence of operations, operations and maintenance documentation, and training needs to support turnover and operational readiness.

- Demonstrate accountability for individual performance and contribution to team and business objectives.

- Identify and recommend opportunities to improve processes, service delivery, and team effectiveness.

- Exercise sound judgment and maintain a high standard of quality, consistency, and professionalism.

- Maintain a professional and customer focused approach in daily interactions and decision making.

- Contribute to a collaborative, results driven team culture through professionalism and effective communication.

- Build effective working relationships with colleagues, vendors, contractors, and external partners.

- Take ownership of assigned work, follow through on commitments, and meet established expectations.

- Seek and apply feedback to support continuous improvement and professional growth.

- Demonstrate flexibility in supporting responsibilities and business needs beyond core job duties when appropriate.

What We Are Looking For:
Required

- Coordinate commissioning activities for assigned projects, project phases, systems, or commissioning scopes.

- Participate in design, construction, owner, vendor, and commissioning meetings to understand project objectives, schedules, risks, and readiness requirements.

- Support development, maintenance, and execution of commissioning plans, schedules, issue logs, testing plans, and project documentation.

- Collaborate with design, construction, operations, vendors, contractors, and third-party commissioning providers to support successful project execution.

- Assist in identifying commissioning risks, schedule constraints, and testing readiness concerns and communicate them to project stakeholders.

-
Testing & Operational Readiness

- Support readiness planning and execution activities for Level 3, Level 4, and Integrated Systems Testing (IST).

- Participate in site-based commissioning activities to help verify successful execution, document testing results, and support issue resolution.

- Coordinate testing activities among contractors, vendors, project teams, operations personnel, and commissioning providers.

- Monitor testing progress and help ensure issues, deficiencies, and retesting requirements are properly documented and resolved.

- Support efforts to verify systems are commissioned in accordance with project requirements, design intent, and operational expectations.

-
Owner Representative Responsibilities

- Represent CyrusOne during assigned commissioning activities and testing events.

- Support management of the commissioning process from the owner's perspective while coordinating with third-party commissioning providers.

- Hold contractors, vendors, and commissioning partners accountable for assigned scope, schedule commitments, testing requirements, and documentation deliverables.

- Identify gaps in testing execution, documentation quality, operational readiness, and issue resolution.

- Communicate project risks, testing concerns, documentation deficiencies, and schedule impacts to project stakeholders.

- Support alignment among design intent, construction completion, commissioning execution, and operations handoff activities.

-
Project Reporting & Issue Management

- Track commissioning deficiencies, open issues, action items, retesting requirements, and closeout activities through completion.

- Provide regular project status updates regarding testing readiness, issue resolution, documentation status, and turnover risks.

- Maintain accurate commissioning records and project documentation.

- Support development of commissioning reports and project closeout summaries.

- Collaborate with project teams to resolve issues affecting startup, testing, turnover, or operational readiness.

-
Project Closeout & Operational Handoff

- Coordinate closeout documentation for assigned projects and commissioning scopes.

- Work with contractors, vendors, commissioning providers, project managers, and operations teams to gather and review turnover documentation.

- Track completion of testing reports, punch list items, substantial completion documentation, occupancy-related documentation, operating manuals, warranties, as-built drawings, spare parts inventories, and other closeout deliverables.

- Support completion of commissioning closeout packages within established project timelines.

- Ensure project documentation is properly reviewed, organized, stored, and transferred to operations teams for long-term use.

- Facilitate successful transition from commissioning to operational ownership.

Education / Certifications :

- Bachelor’s Degree in Mechanical, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science or equivalent work experience

Minimum   Requirements:

- 3-5 years of experience in commissioning, construction management, facility operations, startup, testing, project management, or a related technical field.

- Experience supporting commissioning, turnover, startup, testing, construction closeout, or operational readiness activities for complex facilities.

- Working knowledge of mechanical, electrical, controls, and critical infrastructure systems.

- Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, specifications, test procedures, commissioning plans, and operating sequences.

- Experience coordinating activities among contractors, vendors, consultants, and cross-functional project teams.

- Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, and competing stakeholder requirements.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate technical information to both technical and non-technical audiences.

- Demonstrated attention to detail and commitment to documentation quality.

- Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite, including Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Teams.

- Experience using Bluebeam or similar document management and review software.

- Ability to travel 50 to 75%

-

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience supporting commissioning activities for data centers, mission-critical facilities, healthcare, industrial, manufacturing, utility, or similarly complex environments.

- Familiarity with Level 3, Level 4, and Integrated Systems Testing (IST).

- Experience supporting owner-representative, commissioning, construction management, or facility operations teams.

- Knowledge of commissioning issue tracking, deficiency management, turnover, and project closeout processes.

- Experience using commissioning management software, reporting tools, or project management platforms.

- Understanding of substantial completion, system turnover, warranty management, and operations handoff activities.

- CAPM, PMP, CxA, CCP, CBCP, or other relevant industry certifications.

title: Critical Environments Operator (Level 1-4)
location_raw: Aurora, IL; Wood Dale, IL; Lombard, IL
description:
About the Role

We are building a pipeline of talented Critical Environments Operators across all experience levels — from associates just starting their careers in data center operations to seasoned lead technicians ready to mentor others and drive operational excellence.

As a Critical Environments Operator at CyrusOne, you will be part of a 24/7/365 Operations & Maintenance team responsible for keeping mission-critical data center infrastructure running at peak reliability. You will operate, monitor, and maintain electrical, mechanical, and HVAC/R systems while upholding the highest standards of safety, workmanship, and customer service.

Whether you are early in your career or bringing years of hands-on experience, there is a place for you here — and a clear path forward.

What You Will Do

- Monitor and operate data center mechanical, electrical, and HVAC/R systems to ensure continuous uptime and reliability

- Respond to building system alarms, prioritizing critical load protection, equipment preservation, and root cause analysis

- Execute Preventive Maintenance work orders and follow SOPs, MOPs, EOPs, and MMRs as appropriate

- Use a Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) to track work orders, labor hours, and PMs

- Coordinate with contractors and vendors; enforce Lockout/Tagout and other safety protocols

- Perform equipment and system operational modifications, including critical switching and safe working area setup

- Maintain awareness of and compliance with all company, government, and client policies, procedures, and EHS requirements

- At senior levels: provide mentorship to junior operators, lead critical switching events, and participate in capacity planning and reporting

Levels & Experience
This is an evergreen posting that supports hiring across four levels. The right level for you will be determined based on your experience and qualifications during the interview process.

- Level I:
No prior data center experience required. Ideal for candidates eager to learn data center O&M, with 0–2 years in operations, maintenance, or customer service roles. Strong safety mindset and willingness to learn are the most important qualities.

- Level II:
3–5 years of experience in Tier 2, 3, or 4 data centers or a technical facility maintenance role. Entry-level skills in electrical, mechanical, or HVAC/R disciplines — whether through a degree, trade program, or hands-on work experience. Familiarity with CMMS and work order processes a plus.

- Level III:
5–7 years of data center or building engineering experience. Journeyman-level skills in electrical, mechanical, or HVAC/R. Ability to operate independently, troubleshoot systems, stabilize operations during incidents, and guide less experienced team members.

- Level IV:
7+ years of relevant experience with demonstrated expertise at the journeyman or master level. Active HVAC certification or Journeyman/Master Electrician license preferred. Proven ability to lead operational activities, manage vendor relationships, and support team development.

What We Are Looking For

- Strong commitment to safety — always

- Clear verbal and written communication skills

- Solid problem-solving and decision-making ability

- Proficiency with personal computers, including Microsoft Word and Excel

- Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, high-stakes environment

- Willingness to work a flexible schedule, including on-call rotation and extended hours during emergencies

- Team-first mindset — promotes collaboration and shared success

- Desire to provide the highest levels of service to internal and external customers

Work Environment
This role operates in a fast-paced, physically active data center environment. Candidates must be able to lift up to 50 pounds, perform considerable walking, bending, and standing, and be available for 24/7/365 shift work including after-hours emergency response.

Why CyrusOne?

- Career growth   — a defined progression from Associate through Lead Operator and beyond, with ongoing investment in your development

- Cutting-edge work   — support AI, hyperscale, and cloud infrastructure for some of the world's most demanding customers

- Global scale   — be part of a team operating across North America, EMEA, and APAC

- Award-winning culture   — 2026 Top Workplaces USA National Award winner, recognized for our people-first environment

- Values-driven   — everything we do is grounded in CARE: Commitment, Accountability, Respect, and Excellence

title: Controls Field Engineer
location_raw: Sterling, VA; Aurora, IL; Durham, NC; Chandler, AZ
description:
The Controls Field Engineer supports the availability, reliability, and day-to-day operation of EPMS and BMS control systems across assigned data center sites within a defined region.

This role is field-forward and operationally grounded, serving as the on-site, regional technical resource for controls system health, troubleshooting, documentation, and commissioning.

The Field Controls Engineer works closely with Operational Controls Systems, Site Operations, Regional Operations Directors (RODs), and IT Operations teams to ensure control systems accurately represent electrical and mechanical infrastructure, remain stable and secure, and support 24×7 mission critical operations.

Key Responsibilities
Controls Systems Operations & Support

- Support the availability and reliability of EPMS, BMS, and associated control systems across assigned sites.

- Perform routine system checks, alarm reviews, and health validations to ensure data accuracy and system stability.

- Troubleshoot controls-related issues across software, network, and field device layers.

- Execute approved changes, patches, and minor upgrades under established change management processes.

- Maintain backups, configuration records, and system access controls.

Field Engineering & Commissioning Support

- Support commissioning, cutovers, energizations, and retrofits from a controls perspective.

- Perform point-to-point checks, basic logic validation, and graphics verification.

- Assist with meter, relay, sensor, and controller integration and validation.

- Capture and maintain as-built documentation following field work.

Electrical & Systems Awareness

- Read and interpret one-line diagrams, electrical schematics, and control drawings.

- Validate that EPMS/BMS hierarchies reflect real-world electrical and mechanical configurations.

- Partner with electrical and mechanical SMEs to correct discrepancies and improve monitoring fidelity.

Documentation & Procedures

- Create and maintain SOPs, MOPs, EOPs, control narratives, and system diagrams as assigned.

- Ensure system inventories, naming conventions, and point mappings remain accurate.

- Contribute to regional standards for alarms, graphics, and documentation.

Cross-Functional Coordination‑Functional Coordination

- Act as a technical liaison between Operations Controls Systems, Site Operations, and IT Operations.

- Coordinate troubleshooting efforts that span controls software, networking, and physical infrastructure.

- Work with IT Ops on server hosting, virtualization, network connectivity, and security requirements related to controls systems.

Regional Coverage & On-Call

- Support a defined geographic region (e.g., NVA, NYM, and DUR).

- Participate in on-call rotations for controls-related incidents.

- Travel up to ~25% to support commissioning, outages, and regional projects.

Required Qualifications

- 4–6+ years of experience in industrial controls, facilities automation, or mission critical environments (data center experience preferred).

- Hands‑on experience supporting EPMS, BMS, or BAS platforms.

Preferred Qualifications

- Prior data center experience supporting 24×7 operations.

- Commissioning or startup experience in electrical or mechanical control systems.

- Experience with platforms such as Delta, Ignition, ALC, Schneider, Eaton, or similar.

- Comfort working at the intersection of software, networking, and physical infrastructure.

Competencies

- Strong hands-on troubleshooter with practical electrical intuition

- Comfortable working in live, mission critical environments.

- Detail-oriented with disciplined documentation habits.

- Calm, collaborative, and operationally focused.

- Able to balance site-level urgency with regional consistency.

title: Energy Policy & Regulatory Affairs Manager

The successful candidate will possess a strong understanding of the energy industry, including utility regulation, energy infrastructure, wholesale and retail energy markets, renewable energy development, and public policy issues affecting data center growth and operations.

Responsibilities:

Business Support & Strategic Analysis

title: Senior Data Center Facilities Specialist
description:
The Senior Data Center Facilities Specialist is an administrative position responsible for leading front-end coordination, governance, and performance oversight of facility operations. This role ensures operational excellence by managing workflows, monitoring performance, auditing maintenance execution, owning RFC and MOP coordination, leading customer engagement, and driving compliance across site activities.

This position does not perform hands-on maintenance, equipment operation, or physical troubleshooting. All operational execution, including equipment manipulation or state changes, is performed by designated Operations Engineering personnel.

This role is designated for CHI & NYM sites only.

Operational Coordination & Visibility (Daily)

- Maintain ownership of site operational status, including impaired equipment, active incidents, and ongoing work activities.

- Own internal and customer-facing communications cadence to ensure consistent, timely communication.

- Ensure visibility into daily site activity (e.g., vendor presence, scheduled maintenance) and confirm required notifications have been distributed.

- Review system dashboards (BMS/EPMS, monitoring platforms) to identify trends or anomalies; drive follow-up actions with responsible teams.

- Own resolution of open customer and internal service requests, ensuring progress and communication cadence.

- Lead interior and exterior building assessments (visual only) and direct Operations Engineering to execute corrective action.

Performance Monitoring & Compliance (Weekly)

- Own tracking of planned maintenance and repair completion against established schedules and standards.

- Own the PM audit program (e.g., JLL quarterly chiller PM); confirm thresholds and drive remediation when gaps are identified.

- Own work documentation quality at the site; drive correction with responsible teams.

- Review operational logs, reports, and documentation to ensure quality, accountability, and adherence to expectations.

- Drive coordination with planning, scheduling, and site leadership to execute against the annual maintenance plan.

- Own the site risk register; escalate to Chief Engineer and leadership.

Audit, Reporting & Data Integrity (Monthly)

- Own administrative audits of systems, records, and asset data to ensure accuracy and completeness.

- Own inventory reconciliation in coordination with operational teams; ensure documentation reflects current state.

- Own site performance metrics and KPI narrative; surface trends, gaps, and opportunities to leadership.

- Own regulatory, environmental, and operational documentation completeness and compliance.

- Lead site inspection readiness; coordinate reviews and represent the site in findings discussions.

Governance & Documentation (Quarterly & Ongoing)

- Own oversight of operational procedures and documentation (EOPs, SOPs, MOPs); ensure accuracy, version control, and accessibility.

- Own audit readiness; organize and provide required documentation for internal and external reviews.

- Own review of site drawings, escalation processes, and supporting materials for accuracy and alignment with operational standards.

- High attention to detail in documentation and compliance tracking.

title: Facility Manager
description:
The Facility Manager is responsible for ensuring optimal performance of data center and facility environments, systems and personnel, as well as, the daily over-site and guidance for administrative and maintenance functions.

Essential Functions:
Environmental Management

- Manage day to day operations of cooling (production & distribution) and electrical systems

- Troubleshoot issues related to the critical infrastructure using test equipment, observation and automation, monitoring and control applications

- Proactively develop and implement maintenance activities to include both critical infrastructure and general maintenance of the physical plant (appearance)

- Work with Operations and Sales leadership to assure all environmental issues are handled and communicated correctly to the customer

- Report on all SLA required activities

Capacity Management

- Maintain current status and future status reporting on all capacity thresholds within the facility

Access Management

- Work with Security Manager to assure all access points are monitored and controlled

- In conjunction with Security Manager, manage all security issues to resolution and conduct post mortems

Building Management

- Management of the building and its related services such as janitorial, grounds, plumbing, fuel, phone systems, etc.

- Manage all sub-contractor agreements to maintain the facility

- Operation and maintenance of cable plant and fiber entrance, raised floor systems, automation and control systems, fire detection and suppression systems and security systems

- Develop and document operational standards, maintenance schedules, training and testing procedures, emergency contacts, inventory requirements and vendor relationships

Environmental Services Management

- Set up and maintain environmental monitoring solutions for all managed facilities

- Work with Operations to assure monitoring is in place for delivered services

Asset Management

- Management of asset tracking processes and systems

Support of Customer Implementations

- Work with Implementation Manager to assure a smooth implementation process for the customer

- Review and close tickets

- Design and create service delivery procedural manual

- Oversee training and development process for service delivery group

- Participate in 24 X 7 X 365 rotation

Minimum Requirements:

- Extensive experience and knowledge of electrical and mechanical equipment and systems operations and maintenance including, but not limited to, Caterpillar generator sets, Square D paralleling gear, MGE UPS systems, Trane Chiller plants and pumps, smoke detection systems and fire alarm systems

- Cable plant design and management

- Experience with building automation, monitoring and control systems (i.e. Trane Tracer Summit, SquareD PowerLogic, Caterpillar/ISO Power Lynx and Eaton Foreseer)

- Energy audits

- Project management

- AutoCad & Visio a plus

- Knowledge of building automation, monitoring and control systems including Trane Tracer Summit, SquareD PowerLogic, and Caterpillar/ISO Power Lynx

- Energy audits

- Ability to work well with all facility personnel and delegate tasks appropriately

- Strong customer service skills

- Excellent oral and written communication skills

- Ability to develop and document procedures and train other personnel

What You Will Do:

- Manage and maintain the CMMS (Computerized Maintenance Management System) to track, prioritize, and close work orders with accuracy

- Coordinate with Operations, Engineering, and vendors to ensure maintenance activities are completed on time and with minimal impact

- Lead asset audits and ensure accurate data integrity within the CMMS system

- Monitor and manage spare parts inventory, including sourcing and procurement planning

- Support capital projects and assist with planning site outages and maintenance shutdowns

- Develop and improve maintenance processes, SOPs (Standard Operating Procedures), and job plans

- Conduct root cause analysis on maintenance issues and support continuous improvement initiatives

What We Are Looking For:
Required

- Minimum 3+ years of maintenance planner/scheduler experience

- Minimum 3–5+ years of industrial, data center, or related maintenance experience
